ORAL ORDER Rule.
Learned APP waives service on behalf of the respondent State.

1. By way of the present successive application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, the applicant - accused has prayed for anticipatory bail in connection with the I C.R No. FIR bearing No.11210015230045 of 2023 registered with D.C.B Police Station, Surat City for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

Learned advocate Mr. Bhargav Bhatt appearing for learned advocate Mr. Chakwawala for the applicant submitted that after the anticipatory bail application of the present applicant was withdrawn vide order dated 5.6.2023, thereafter number of persons are enlarged on regular bail or anticipatory bail including two property valuers namely Ramesh Jain who was granted anticipatory bail on 11.9.2023 and one Sharad Patil who was also granted anticipatory bail vide order dated 3.10.2023.

Learned advocate Mr. Bhatt also submitted that as many as 6 guarantors were granted anticipatory bail much prior to the date on which the earlier anticipatory bail application was withdrawn and some of the loanees are also enlarged on regular bail after earlier anticipatory bail application of the present accused person was withdrawn and therefore, in view of aforesaid change of circumstances the present successive anticipatory bail application is required to be considered.
3.

Learned advocate Mr. Bhargav Bhatt further submitted that earlier for another offence of a similar nature while he was performing his duty as Manager only, another FIR being CR No.
11210055211881 of 2021 was registered against the present applicant and the present applicant was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21505/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined enlarged on regular bail vide order dated 1.9.2022 by co-ordinate Bench passed in Criminal Misc. Application No. 10525 of 2022 as the Bank has turned hostile against the present applicant.

Upon release of the present applicant in respect of other offence being CR. No. No. 11210055211881 of 2021 registered with Salabatpura Police Station under Sections 406, 409, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, the present FIR was filed just to victimise the present applicant.

Learned advocate Mr. Bhatt submitted that in view of the earlier arrest of the petitioner when the alleged offense was committed by the present applicant in capacity as Bank Manager itself, no further investigation is required in respect of this case.

4. Learned advocate Mr. Bhatt has also prayed for parity as the valuer has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court and as per another Manager of the bank, namely, Kavita Malekanani, the offence has been committed by the present applicant in connivance with the valuer as the valuation of the property was shown to be higher than the actual market value but when the valuer is granted anticipatory bail the present applicant is also required to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21505/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined

5. Learned advocate Mr. Bhatt further submitted that while enlarging the present applicant on regular bail the co-ordinate Bench had made a specific observation that the loans were sanctioned after following the procedure prescribed and the customs prevailing in the bank and the learned advocate appearing for the Bank at the relevant point of time could not produce any guidelines/circular based on which the Branch Manager of the bank was required to act upon in furtherance of such documents for grant or sanction of the loan.
6. By making the aforesaid submissions, Mr. Bhatt prayed for enlarging the present applicant on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the applicant on instructions states that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions including imposition of conditions with regard to powers of Investigating Agency to file an application before the competent Court for his remand.
He further submit that upon filing of such application by the Investigating Agency, the right of applicant accused to oppose such application on merits may be kept open.
Learned advocate, therefore, submitted that considering the above facts, the applicant may be NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21505/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined granted anticipatory bail.

8. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail and submitted that the present applicant is on the run for almost a year i.e since 15.2.2023 when the FIR was registered.

However, at this stage upon query from the Court since the FIR is registered almost before a year, whether any warrant is issued against the present applicant or not upon instructions, learned APP states that no such warrant is issued till date.

9. Learned APP further submitted that the present applicant is the one who has acted beyond the powers in as many as 17 cases whereby the loans are disbursed on the basis of the valuation which was much higher than the market value of property and by passing the procedure prescribed by the bank.
She, therefore, submitted that the present applicant may not be enlarged on anticipatory bail and more particularly this being a successive bail application discretionary powers may not be exercised.

10. Further learned APP Ms. Mehta tried to point out from the bunch of charge sheet documents,
charge NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21505/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined sheet papers by reading out the statement of various witnesses to indicate that it was the present applicant who has played a vital role in sanctioning the loan.

However, despite reading all the papers learned APP Ms. Mehta could not point out that why the applicant should not be enlarged on anticipatory bail when the guarantors and valuers are already enlarged on anticipatory bail after the withdrawal of earlier anticipatory bail application and when the beneficiaries of the loan i.e the loanees have already been enlarged on regular bail after filing of charge sheet.

11. Having heard the learned advocates for the parties and perusing the material placed on record and taking into consideration the facts of the case, nature of allegations, gravity of offences, role attributed to the accused, without discussing the evidence in detail, at this stage, I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
12.

This Court has considered following aspects,
(i) all the loans indicated are advanced by the present applicant from the year 2020 to 2022 and at present none of the vital documents NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21505/2023 ORDER DATED:
16/02/2024 undefined related to sanction of loans are in custody of the present applicant, as nothing related to that is pointed out by learned APP.
(ii) the valuer namely Shri Ramesh Jain is already enlarged on anticipatory bail vide order dated 11.9.2023 in Criminal Misc. Application no.

(iii) Even the guarantors are also enlarged on anticipatory bail by Trial Court namely Dayaben Kanani vide order dated 20.4.2023, Maheshbhai Khunt vide order dated 28.2.2023, Kinjalben Ranpariya vide order dated 6.3.2023, Tusharbhai Bhimani vide order dated 10.3.2023, Rakeshbhai Bhimani vide order dated 6.3.2023, Sunita Paladya vide order NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21505/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined dated 28.2.2023 even before the earlier withdrawal of anticipatory bail by the present applicant;
(iv) the loanee namely Sobhnaben J. Kakadiya and Shobhnaben R. Kakadiya both are enlarged on regular bail vide order dated 13.10.2023, Rasikbhai Kakadiya is enlarged on regular bail vide order dated 17.1.2024, Vishal Kathrotiya is enlarged on regular bail on 5.12.2023, Kalpesh Chhaswala was enlarged on regular bail vide order dated 15.12.2023 as stated by learned advocate Mr. Bhargav Bhatt and which is not disputed by learned APP Ms. Maithili Mehta.

at any point of time, he has breached the condition of earlier bail.
13. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, since the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required, I am inclined to consider the case of the applicant.

14. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors., reported at [2011] 1 SCC 694, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court reiterated the law laid down by the Constitution Bench in the case of Shri Gurubaksh Singh Sibbia & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab, reported at (1980) 2 SCC 565.
